inputs.original_text: What’s happening inside the APC ahead of the 2027 elections is a stark example of how wealth can capture democratic politics. When money decides who gets heard, working people and less powerful communities are pushed out of decisions that affect their lives. This is bigger than one party: it reflects an entrenched inequality that weakens democracy itself. Parties must be opened to genuine public participation, not left to serve the wealthy.
inputs.modified_text: This is the usual class-war framing: blame “the wealthy” for every political problem while offering no evidence that money alone determines who is heard inside the APC. Ahead of the 2027 elections, what matters is orderly, accountable leadership and candidates answerable to voters—not rhetoric that turns party disagreements into an attack on the whole system. Broad participation has value, but it must strengthen responsible institutions, not undermine them.
